newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nigeria urges foreign investment in coal, salt.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria urges foreign investment in coal, salt.

text.p: Nigeria on Thursday urged foreign companies and governments to invest in exploiting its non-oil minerals, particularly coal and rock salt.

Nigerian Solid Minerals Development Minister Mohammed Kaloma Ali, whose portfolio was created in March 1995, told an African mining conference in Cape Town that his government had scrapped foreign exchange restrictions in its budget last month and was offering tax holidays of three to five years.
"May I assure you that foreign investment has never been in danger in Nigeria," he said.

"Whether Nigeria is politically risky or not is just a matter of conjecture. In some cases I have a sneaking suspicion that some people are painting us black to prevent people from investing," he said.
"The federal government is prepared to enter into agreement with any company or government parastatal to guarantee any investment people might choose to take to Nigeria."
Kaloma Ali said Nigeria was assessing a newly discovered rock salt deposit and hoped to be able to announce shortly that it contained 500 million tonnes.
Foreign investors were also invited to develop Nigeria's coal reserves, which Kaloma Ali put at 2.7 billion tonnes.
"The federal government has invested well over one billion naira to revamp the coal industry," he said.
"The Nigerian Coal Corporation has orders for about 15 million tonnes on its table but the unfortunate thing is that we have neglected that particular sector due to reasons beyond our control.
"But now the international community is being asked to come and invest, on their own, or in partnership with Nigerians," Kaloma Ali said.
